content: If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Take this medication by mouth, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily. If stomach upset occurs, take it with food. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, weight, response to treatment, and any other medications you may be taking. For optimal effectiveness, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve before completing the course. Common side effects may include diarrhea, stomach upset, changes in taste, nausea, or vomiting. This medication may also cause discoloration of urine, sweat, saliva, or tears to a brown-orange color. This effect is harmless and will resolve once the medication is discontinued. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking rifabutin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other rifamycins (such as rifampin), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Rifabutin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (such as the typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. If you have HIV, be aware that breast milk can transmit HIV to your baby. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Rifabutin can accelerate the removal of other medications from your body, potentially affecting their effectiveness. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, which could result in pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (such as liver function tests and complete blood counts) should be performed regularly to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Be sure to keep all medical and laboratory appointments.
